edges.description: The route from the astrocyte volume defect to water between myelin lamellae is the accepted account of MLC but the intermediate steps are not established, and in this form the vacuolation has only been shown in mice carrying a dominant allele. The step is also not sufficient as drawn: astrocyte-specific loss of the VRAC pore subunit LRRC8A does not produce the lesion.

edges.target: Diffuse Swelling of Cerebral White Matter

edges.description: Brain enlargement is attributed to the white matter edema; the intermediate steps are not established.

The subcortical fluid spaces arise in the most swollen white matter. In this form they are often only near-cystic rarefaction rather than true cysts, and how either forms from the vacuolating process has not been studied.
Early mild motor delay is attributed to the white matter edema; the intermediate steps are not known.
Residual clumsiness after the edema resolves is attributed to the early white matter disease; mechanism unknown.

Seizures are infrequent in this form. In the MLC mouse models disturbed astrocyte ion and water handling lowers the seizure threshold, but that work was done in Mlc1-null and Glialcam-null animals rather than in a dominant allele, so the link here is inferred.
The same lesion resolves rather than progressing, which is the defining feature of this disease; the account in the downstream node is a hypothesis about why.
Hypothesis. The stable cognitive impairment of this disease does not follow the resolving edema, and GlialCAM has developmental functions in astrocytes, but nothing connects the two.

nodes.description: A candidate second route, outside the endfoot volume-regulation complex, for the developmental part of the phenotype. In astrocytes of the developing mouse cortex, dominant hepaCAM variants from both structural groups redistribute the protein across the cell and change its interaction partners, with less association with Connexin 43 and ClC-2 and with the potassium channel KCNQ2. GlialCAM also controls astrocyte territory, branching and gap junction coupling in mouse cortex. Intellectual disability and autistic features are more frequent in this disease than in classic MLC, which fits a function of GlialCAM separate from its endfoot role, but no study has connected any of these changes to the cognitive or behavioural phenotype.

nodes.description: Expressed alongside wild-type GlialCAM, a dominant IgV allele reduces the fraction of wild-type GlialCAM that reaches cell-cell junctions, which a recessive MLC2A allele does not do. Two structural routes produce the same result. Group D1 alleles (p.Gly89Ser, p.Gly89Asp, p.Arg92Trp) sit in the cis dimerization segment and also lose the ability to bind GlialCAM in the same cell; group D2 alleles (p.Gln56Pro, p.Ser59Asn, p.Asp128Asn) keep normal homo-oligomerization and instead map to the surface modelled as the trans interface between GlialCAM on apposed cells. Both groups mislocalize GlialCAM itself, as recessive alleles also do, so the dominance lies in the effect on the normal allele's product rather than in the mutant protein's own destination.

nodes.description: CRISPR knock-in of the recurrent dominant patient allele in the single copy patients carry. White matter vacuolation appears in the anterior commissure within the first month and then declines over following months, which is the animal counterpart of the human remission, while cerebellar vacuolation appears at 3 months and increases. Glialcam immunofluorescence is reduced but no clear mislocalization was seen. No MRI abnormality was detected at any age.

Knock-in of the dominant patient allele G89S. Only the heterozygote matches the human genotype, and it shows an intermediate picture, with MLC1 diffusely distributed in the cerebellar molecular layer, only a little left along Bergmann glia processes, ClC-2 retained in Bergmann glia somata, and the mildest myelin vacuolation of all the lines studied. The homozygote, to which no patient corresponds, has the full mislocalization phenotype and cerebellar vacuoles, and shows that the mutant protein keeps part of its ability to stabilize MLC1.

nodes.description: A single heterozygous missense variant in exon 2 of HEPACAM, encoding the first immunoglobulin (IgV) domain of GlialCAM, is the whole genetic lesion; the second allele is wild type. Eleven of the 29 GLIALCAM variants known from MLC patients act dominantly, all of them in exon 2 and all missense except one single-codon deletion. The variant is inherited from a parent in about four fifths of cases and arises de novo in the rest. The recurrent allele is p.Arg92Trp, and the same residue also carries the recessive MLC2A allele p.Arg92Gln, so the amino acid substituted rather than the position decides the mode of inheritance.

nodes.description: With less MLC1 and ClC-2 at the endfoot membrane, astrocytes activate the volume-regulated anion current poorly and recover less well from swelling, which is the cellular defect common to every genetic form of MLC. No study has measured regulatory volume decrease in cells carrying a single dominant GLIALCAM allele, so this node is carried over from MLC1-related and GlialCAM knock-down work and is expected to be milder here. How much of the disease this node carries is open: deleting the essential VRAC pore subunit LRRC8A from astrocytes leaves volume recovery normal in situ and produces no white matter edema, so a deficit of VRAC conductance by itself is not what produces the lesion.

nodes.description: GlialCAM is the subunit that brings MLC1 out of the endoplasmic reticulum to astrocyte-astrocyte junctions at perivascular and subpial endfeet, and it also targets the ClC-2 chloride channel to those junctions and changes its gating. Dominant GlialCAM alleles do not weaken binding to MLC1 or to ClC-2 and still modify ClC-2 currents, so the defect is one of position: with less GlialCAM at junctions, less MLC1 and ClC-2 are there too. The reduction is partial rather than complete, because one wild-type allele is expressed and the mutant protein retains part of its chaperone activity, which is the usual explanation for the milder course.

evidence.reference_title: Expanding the spectrum of megalencephalic leukoencephalopathy with subcortical cysts in two patients with GLIALCAM mutations.
evidence.snippet: The first patient has MLC2B disease, as shown by the improvement in MRI and clinical parameters. In this case, we identified a novel GLIALCAM mutation (p.Q56P) which affected the localization of GlialCAM and its associated subunits, however activating ClC-2 function as the wild-type protein.

nodes.description: Dominant cis-interface allele with incorrect junctional localization and impaired homo-oligomerization. It is the allele knocked into the Glialcam(dn) mouse line, which with the p.Arg92Trp knock-in is one of only two in vivo models of a dominant GLIALCAM variant.
